title: The Thirsty Pigeon
summary: Across the rocky pastures and olive orchards of ancient Greece, a memorable encounter unfolded. Through unexpected trial and turning point, each character learns that blind haste born of desperate desire leads straight into destruction.
full_text: Across the rocky pastures and olive orchards of ancient Greece, a memorable encounter unfolded. A pigeon, tormented by a raging thirst on a scorching summer day, flew frantically over the rooftops in search of water. The surrounding valley lay quiet in the midday heat, yet within the peaceful scene, natural instincts and rival interests were quietly at work. Before long, the initial quiet gave way to a sharp challenge as unexpected circumstances forced both sides to act. Every fountain was dry, and the gutters were filled with dust. Glancing toward the wall of a tavern, the desperate bird saw a large sign depicting a crystal glass brim-full of sparkling, ice-cold water, painted with such exquisite realism by an artist that water droplets seemed to glisten upon its rim. Each party sought to press their advantage, weighing spoken words against unspoken motives. When the decisive moment arrived, neither boastful pretense nor hasty excuses could alter the outcome. Deluded by his frantic desire and without stopping to inspect the scene, the pigeon closed his wings and swooped down with reckless speed, intending to plunge into the refreshing vessel. He slammed headfirst into the hard wooden signboard with a resounding CRACK! The impact broke his wings and shattered his breastbone. Tumbling helpless to the cobblestones below, the dying bird was promptly picked up by a tavern cat, sighing in his final breath: "Alas, my blind haste made an illusion my executioner!" The experience left behind a timeless truth for all who heard the tale, demonstrating that blind haste born of desperate desire leads straight into destruction.
moral: Blind haste born of desperate desire leads straight into destruction.
